name: Claude Code Meetup For Developers
why: Builders share demos of projects built with Claude Code, followed by a live Q&A with the Anthropic team.

name: Grieving & Weaving
why: Knitting, crocheting, and crafting in a cemetery chapel, sharing stories and grief resources. All skill levels welcome.

name: A Better World Is Possible: Youth Confront Climate Crisis
why: Danica Novgorodoff and Meera Subramanian present their graphic book on global youth climate action, with activists Jamie Margolin and Shiv Soin.

name: Bread + Puppet Theater: The End of the World Never Minding Show
why: Bread + Puppet's spring tour stops in NYC with a new puppet show featuring a revolt orchestra, screaming choirs, and a reckoning with catastrophe.

name: Marcel Duchamp at MoMA
why: The first U.S. retrospective of Duchamp's work since 1973, featuring 300 works spanning his full career from 1900 to 1968.

name: AI Startup Founder Pitch Night
why: Early-stage AI startup founders pitch their ideas to an audience of investors and fellow builders.

name: How Movements Are Built
why: Author Saul Austerlitz moderates a panel with Council Member Alexa Aviles and organizers on what turns private alarm into public action.

name: Julia Wertz: Bury Me Already (It's Nice Down Here)
why: Cartoonist Julia Wertz presents her comic memoir of motherhood during challenging times, in conversation with Emily Gould.

name: The Pickled City: Tasting & Discussion
why: Tasting and discussion tracing the brined cucumber from ancient Mesopotamia to the Lower East Side, with access to the Street Food City exhibition.

name: Jordan Klepper: New Goods
why: Daily Show co-host Jordan Klepper works out new material with comedy pals at this intimate Park Slope venue.

name: Out In Tech: Queer Tech Stories Across Generations
why: Queer technologists share stories spanning generations of LGBTQ+ experience in the tech industry, at Spotify's NYC headquarters.

name: AngularNYC Meetup
why: Monthly Angular developer meetup hosted at Google's NYC office.

name: Dali: The Great Years 1929-1939 (Opening Reception)
why: Opening reception for the most significant Dali exhibition in New York since 2008, spanning his most transformative decade.

name: The Other Art Fair (Opening Night)
why: Opening night access to 120 artists showing original works at the Brooklyn Navy Yard. First dibs before the weekend crowds.

name: Possibilities in Theory
why: Artist Gregg Bordowitz reflects on how French Theory opened new possibilities for New York artists of the 80s and 90s.

name: 2026 Whiting Award Winners Reading
why: This year's Whiting Award winners read from their work, hosted by Sidik Fofana. Wine and cheese served.

name: BAM Free Music: Lena Dardelet
why: French-Dominican singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Lena Dardelet performs in BAM's free Caribbean music series.

name: Facts Machine: Science, Comedy + Trivia
why: Scientists and comedians share stories behind their favorite facts, then test knowledge with trivia. This month's theme: Planet Earth.

name: Toy Story Entirely From Memory
why: Blindly-cast performers attempt to recreate Toy Story on stage with no scripts or rehearsals, incorporating audience-written lines and improvised deleted scenes.

name: Robert Mapplethorpe at Gladstone (Closes Sat)
why: 16 large-scale photographs by Mapplethorpe. Organized with the Mapplethorpe Foundation. Closes Saturday.

name: Keith Haring: On the Street (Closes Sunday!)
why: Last weekend. Two of Haring's painted cars in a former carriage house. Closes April 19.

name: AI Design Challenge: Create Anything
why: Build creative projects with Krea AI at this design challenge hosted by the NYU GenART Club.

name: AI Engineers Game Night
why: Smash Bros, Mario Kart, board games, and conversation with AI engineers.

name: H. P. Lovecraft in Gotham
why: Explore Lovecraft's complicated relationship with New York, where the horror writer lived, struggled, and drew dark inspiration.

name: New Directors/New Films (Closing Weekend)
why: 55th edition of the festival closes this weekend. Last chance to catch emerging filmmakers at MoMA and Lincoln Center.

name: Rheology at Playwrights Horizons
why: A physicist mother and her artist son collaborate on a boundary-pushing experiment about sand, flow, and running out of time. Code SKINTRH for $40 tickets. Ends Apr 20.

name: Czech Animation: The Weird and Wonderful (Closes Sat)
why: Alice, the Pied Piper, and more from the world of Czech animation. Final screenings this Friday and Saturday.

name: NYC Fringe Festival (Final Weekend)
why: 70+ independent plays, musicals, and one-person shows. Final weekend. 100% of box office goes directly to artists.

name: Back Door to Broadway Theater Festival (Closes Sun)
why: 11 new works by playwrights from across the U.S. and U.K. Inaugural festival closes Sunday.

name: Moral Mazes of Kieslowski at Metrograph
why: Three Colors trilogy, the Dekalog series, The Double Life of Veronique, and more from the Polish master. Through Apr 25.

name: NYC Fringe Festival (Final Weekend)
why: 70+ independent shows at 5 venues. Final weekend. Pay-what-you-can for many. 100% of box office to artists.

name: Grand Opening: The Green-House at Green-Wood
why: One-time opening weekend for Green-Wood's brand new visitor center. Workshops, explorations, and programs across the grounds.

name: Dali: The Great Years 1929-1939 (Just Opened)
why: Just opened. Most significant Dali showing in NY since 2008. Paintings, sculpture, and archival material from his most transformative decade.

name: The Mad Mad World of Jonathan Adler (Closes Sunday!)
why: Jonathan Adler's first curatorial role: 60+ works from MAD's collection alongside his own designs. Installation by Simon Doonan. Last weekend.

name: Gouache Florals
why: Paint lush, vibrant florals using gouache in this hands-on beginner-friendly workshop.

name: The Other Art Fair
why: 120 artists from around the world. Four days only at the Navy Yard. Browse, meet artists, buy directly.

name: Art x Fashion at Museum at FIT (Closes Sunday!)
why: Is fashion art? 140+ objects explore how fashion has been a partner, not a follower, of fine art. Last weekend. Free.

name: Brooklyn Museum: Saturday Sketch Club
why: Draw in the galleries with fellow artists, with prompts and guidance from museum educators.

name: The Taverns of New York: Colonial Manhattan Cocktail Tour
why: Walking tour through colonial Manhattan's tavern history with cocktail stops and stories of the city's earliest drinking culture.

name: Rheology at Playwrights Horizons
why: A physicist mother and her artist son in a boundary-pushing experiment about sand, flow, and time. Code SKINTRH for $40 tickets. Closes Apr 20.

name: Content Creators Meetup
why: Networking for content creators and digital storytellers at the Brookfield Place waterfront.

name: Revolutionary Spirits
why: Trolley tour through Revolutionary War history at Green-Wood, then a tasting at Fort Hamilton Distillery where Brooklyn distilling began.

name: Streb: Into Thin Air
why: Extreme action ensemble with trampolines, retractable ramps, and suspended parallel bars. Limited spring run through May 3.

name: Cumulo: A Puppet Journey Through the Sky
why: Nonverbal puppet piece on a cotton candy set with floating cloud islands. Just opened this week; limited run through May 3.

name: Peoples' Symphony: Richard Goode, Piano
why: One of America's most distinguished pianists in an intimate Manhattan setting. World-class classical at bargain prices.

name: La MaMa Moves! Dance Festival
why: Contemporary dance by 15+ artists and companies at La MaMa's 21st annual dance festival. Limited run through May 10.

name: NYC Fringe Festival (Final Day)
why: Final day of 70+ independent shows. Last chance across 5 venues. Pay-what-you-can for many.

name: Birding in Peace at Green-Wood
why: Early morning walk with special pre-opening access. Peak spring migration: warblers, woodpeckers, songbirds among magnolias.

name: Grand Opening: The Green-House at Green-Wood (Day 2)
why: Day two of the opening weekend for Green-Wood's new building with fresh programming.

name: The Mad Mad World of Jonathan Adler (FINAL DAY)
why: Last day. 60+ works curated by Adler with installation by Simon Doonan. Your last chance.

name: The Other Art Fair (Final Day)
why: Last day. 120 artists, original works. May have end-of-fair deals.

name: Keith Haring: On the Street (FINAL DAY)
why: Absolute last day. Haring's painted cars, original works, photographs. Free. Closes tonight.

name: Art x Fashion at Museum at FIT (FINAL DAY)
why: Last day. 140+ objects exploring fashion as art, from the museum's permanent collection. Free.

name: Brooklyn Museum: Forces of Nature
why: Special one-day event: create, move, and renew through art-making, dance, and music across the museum. Free.

name: New Directors/New Films (Final Day)
why: Final day of the 55th edition. Last chance for emerging filmmaker discoveries at MoMA and Lincoln Center.

name: Back Door to Broadway Festival (Final Day)
why: Final day of the inaugural festival. 11 new works by playwrights from the U.S. and U.K.

name: Improv for Communication Skills
why: Use improv techniques to build confidence, listen better, and think on your feet.

name: Cumulo: A Puppet Journey (Sunday)
why: Nonverbal puppet piece following Plum through sentient clouds on cotton candy set. Limited run just started this week.

name: Peoples' Symphony: Dover Quartet
why: Grammy-nominated Dover Quartet. One of the most in-demand chamber ensembles in the world, at bargain prices.
